signals.summary: A wave of calm, mat-and-morning-light yoga framed as a mental-reset ritual rather than a workout, aligning with late-summer back-to-routine. Fully producible as empty mats, studio corners and dawn light without ever showing a body.
signals.why_now: Yoga-With-Adriene continues pushing ritual formats: 'Start the Day Grounded | Morning Yoga' and 'Yoga For Tight Hamstrings & Lower Back' (119.9h). Fresh r/yoga discussion is clustering around yoga-as-emotional-reset: 'Could someone please tell me more about emotions during yoga?' (14.2h) and a positive anxiety/meditation-through-yoga thread (0.9h). Autumn reset gives the mat/morning-light framing seasonal pull.

signals.summary: Hyrox, the mass-participation functional-fitness race, is having a sustained mainstream moment across major outlets. Category-central and fast-moving, but body/competition-dependent; only producible via empty arena equipment (sleds, wall balls, rowers), so producibility is low.
signals.why_now: Two big-outlet explainers landed within 72h: 'What to know about the Hyrox fitness trend - Good Morning America' (71.8h) and the ABC News video version (72.2h), on top of standing coverage: 'Is Hyrox the new CrossFit? - usatoday.com' and 'Inside NYC's obsession with HYROX - nypost.com' (582.9h). A clear, still-accelerating wave.

signals.summary: A back-to-routine sleep-hygiene reset centered on the bedroom as a sanctuary: linens, dim lamps, tea and legs-up-the-wall wind-down. Highly producible through interiors and objects, with zero medical claims and no bodies required.
signals.why_now: Object-led bedroom coverage is fresh: 'We Asked 4 Doctors Which Bed Sheets Help You Sleep Better' - Real Simple (78.9h), pairing with evergreen ritual video 'Legs Up The Wall for Better Sleep' and 'Sleep Better Tonight | 10-Minute Bedtime Flow' from Yoga-With-Adriene. Late-summer-into-autumn back-to-routine makes the sleep-reset framing seasonal. (The r/sleep flood was almost entirely gated medical/support threads.)

signals.summary: A fitness-culture shift away from cardio-grind toward gentler, intuitive, lower-intensity movement. Producible as calm studios, quiet walking paths and mats, though it leans partly on bodies.
signals.why_now: Multiple outlets narrate the same pivot: 'Intuitive Workouts Trend Takes Over Fitness World | Why People Are Moving Beyond Gym Goals' - wionews (246.9h), 'The New Workout Trend That Makes a Case for Doing Less' - ELLE, and 'Forget Cardio and High Calorie Burns... A Surprising Group Fitness Trend Reflects a Major Shift' - Men's Journal. A consistent aesthetic drift rather than a spike.

signals.summary: 'Mobility' as a standalone longevity practice — future-proofing the body with daily joint work. Evergreen and category-central; producible through mats, foam rollers and floor-space in morning light, though the underlying content is body-led.
signals.why_now: A steady drumbeat of mobility-as-longevity service pieces: 'Improved performance, freedom of movement and less pain: how to start a mobility practice' - The Guardian, '14 Mobility Moves Anyone Over 35 Should Add to Their Day' - self.com, and the most recent 'Dr Amir Khan's 3 mobility exercises to reduce stiffness' - Woman & Home (147.4h). Evergreen rather than spiking. (Note: the 'mobility training' feed was heavily polluted with off-topic military-mobility items, all discarded.)
